subject: Conditional capacity credit for 24–36mo prepay — approval path
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Amy Lin <amy@solara.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <carlos.m@solara.com>; Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: conditional capacity credit for 24–36mo prepay

Hi Amy —

Great chatting yesterday. Based on the usage profile you shared, I ran a quick model with our pricing team and we can put forward a conditional capacity-credit structure to make the math work for both sides. High level:

- 24-month prepay: 12% term discount + a one-time 8% capacity credit applied to the first quarter
- 36-month prepay: 16% term discount + a one-time 12% capacity credit applied to the first two quarters
- Capacity credits apply only to committed GPU units and amortize over the credit period; unconsumed credit converts to service credit for the next quarter only

Two important conditions:
1) We need a guaranteed minimum payment schedule (phased frontload: 40% Y1, 60% Y2 for 24mo; 35/35/30 for 36mo).
2) Quarterly usage true-ups with a capped true-up exposure (10% of quarterly commit) to protect both parties.

I attached a draft SOW and a pricing workbook showing the breakpoints. Can you confirm procurement timeline and whether Solara needs PO net-30 or net-45? If you want, I can loop in our finance lead (Ben) and pricing (Kim) for a short call next week to walk through the workbook.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: Solara_SOW_v2.pdf, pricing_workbook.xlsx

From: Amy Lin <amy@solara.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <carlos.m@solara.com>; Solara Procurement <procurement@solara.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: conditional capacity credit for 24–36mo prepay

Jordan —

Thanks for the summary and deck. The numbers look promising, but I need to check two things with our CFO and procurement: 1) we prefer net-45 for multi-year prepay to align with budgeting cadence; 2) any clawback language if we materially underuse the committed units (our usage is seasonal and can drop in Q1).

Two asks before we lock: can you (a) clarify how the capacity credit appears on invoices and (b) confirm that credits don't reduce our support tier eligibility for the duration? Finally — if we push to 36 months, what flexibility do we have to add incremental units at the same price band during Y2?

Happy to do a call with Ben & Kim next Tue afternoon.

Thanks,
Amy Lin
Head of AI Programs | Solara Systems
amy@solara.com

Ben / Kim —

Looping you in. Procurement prefers net-45 and wants clawback language explained. Also need confirmation re: support tier impact and incremental unit add-on pricing mid-contract. Call scheduled Tue 25 May 2:00pm PT with Solara (Amy + Carlos).

Key asks:
- Ben: confirm net-45 feasible and propose invoice language for capacity credits (line-item vs. percentage).
- Kim: confirm whether we can price incremental units at committed band if added in Y2, and propose acceptable clawback thresholds.

Thanks — Jordan

Cc: Amy Lin <amy@solara.com>, Carlos Mendes <carlos.m@solara.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: conditional capacity credit for 24–36mo prepay

Jordan / team —

Notes from finance for tomorrow's call:
- Net-45 is OK if legal approves the payment schedule in the SOW; we'll need a signed SOW before we extend net-45 terms.
- Capacity credit will appear as a separate invoice line: "Capacity Credit (one-time)" with a negative amount applied in the first billing cycle(s). We do not net it against support fees.
- Clawback: propose a materiality threshold where underuse >35% of committed units over any rolling 2-quarter period triggers refund/recapture of remaining unamortized credits; but propose a safety cap so Solara's aggregate exposure is limited to 25% of the total prepay value across the contract. This gives both predictability and protection.

I am comfortable with incremental units being added at the committed band if the customer agrees to a 30-day notice to allow capacity planning; pricing for large expansions (>25% of committed units) should be re-reviewed.

I'll join the call tomorrow to confirm wording.

Ben Carter
Head of Finance | Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Amy Lin <amy@solara.com>, Carlos Mendes <carlos.m@solara.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 14:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Notes and next steps from call — capacity credit & terms

Amy / Carlos —

Thanks for the call. Quick recap and agreed next steps:

- Solara prefers the 36-month structure if we can provide the 12% capacity credit and net-45 payment terms.
- Redwood can offer the 36-month: 16% term discount + 12% one-time capacity credit applied over first two quarters, subject to finance/legal sign-off on net-45 and clawback language.
- Ben will draft concise invoice language and clawback clause; Kim will prepare an addendum for mid-contract adds and pricing bands.
- Action items: Ben to circulate suggested invoice wording by Thu EOD; Kim to share addendum draft by Fri. Jordan to circulate an updated SOW with phased payment schedule.

Best,
Jordan

Attachments: redwood_prepay_terms_v1.docx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Amy Lin <amy@solara.com>, Carlos Mendes <carlos.m@solara.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Conditional capacity credit for 24–36mo prepay — approval path

Jordan / team —

I've reviewed Ben's clawback mechanics and Kim's addendum language. I'm approving an exception to our standard prepay guardrails to allow net-45 on this deal given strategic fit and expected ARR. Approval is conditional on two items being completed prior to signature:

1) Legal to insert a unilateral true-up cap (customer-friendly) that limits recapture to 25% of total prepay value; finance to ensure amortization schedule reflects the cap.
2) Procurement to accept the phased frontload schedule (35/35/30 for 36mo) in writing (email confirmation or PO).

Once the above are satisfied, Jordan — please send the final SOW to Amy with DocuSign and mark the deal ready in CRM.

Marissa Cole
VP Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
